messages:
Kenny (CS): FYI — uploading a quick spend heatmap for NovaHealth ahead of their renewal QBR next Wed. Need a short pulse: top drivers, any anomalies, and suggested mitigations before the deck. Link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/nh-spend-heatmap
Emma (CSM): Thanks — skimmed it. Looks like an embedding-heavy spike on 3/12 that doubled daily tokens. Not reflected in usage alerts.
Jack (FinOps): I pulled the cost slice. Embeds are ~62% of yesterday's spend for that account. I can run a per-route cost breakdown if you want.
Priya (SE): Can you paste the top routes? I want to check if the spike aligns with the new batch-embed job we shipped last month.
Kenny (CS): good call. quick sample from the heatmap (top 3 by token delta):
```
route: /v1/embeddings/batch  tokens: +1.2M  calls: +4k
route: /v1/chat/generate      tokens: +300k  calls: +1.1k
route: /v1/embeddings/single  tokens: +80k   calls: +900
```
Emma (CSM): that first route matches the customer script that bulk-sends user vectors. They recently increased batch size to 128. Might be the cause.
Jack (FinOps): Recommendation: set an interim alert for route-level token rate + a soft quota to cap overnight consumption. We can propose a credits-smoothing plan for the QBR (e.g., temporary top-up + optimization tasks).
Priya (SE): For immediate relief: reduce default batch size in their SDK config to 64 and enable prefix KV caching on retrieval calls. I can open a PR with the config change and a migration note.
Kenny (CS): @Emma can you own the customer ask for a temporary credit top-up? @Jack please prepare the per-route cost slide (USD delta) for the QBR. Priya, thanks — plz share PR link and a one-liner impact estimate.
Emma (CSM): On it. I'll ask for a 30% credits buffer for two weeks and include the business justification (search resiliency during the migration).
Jack (FinOps): Slide will include: baseline avg daily spend, spike delta, projected monthly impact if batch remains at 128, and mitigations cost delta. Will have numbers by EOD Fri.
analytics-bot: Automated note — anomaly detected 2026-03-12 04:32Z for account NovaHealth: token-rate z-score 4.1 on route /v1/embeddings/batch. Alerting disabled.
Priya (SE): Quick thought — add a per-customer admission control rule to block >X tokens/min for new batch jobs by default. We can make it opt-out for mature accounts. Low engineering effort, high safety.
Kenny (CS): Solid. Action items summary: Emma -> request temporary top-up and notify customer; Jack -> build per-route cost slide; Priya -> PR for default batch size + admission control proposal; Me -> add alert rule request to ops and schedule a 20-min pre-QBR sync Monday.
Emma (CSM): I'll draft the customer note and include a recommended usage dashboard they can check.
Jack (FinOps): Also adding a quick playbook slide: "if embed spend spikes, check batch sizes, look for bulk backfills, toggle cache, temp top-up."
Kenny (CS): Great. If anyone spots more anomalies in the heatmap before EOD, drop them here. :thumbsup:
